subject: Pilot qualification: air-gapped network, PII retention & egress clarifications
messages:
From: Evan Brooks <evan@medtechlabs.io>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.example> , priyom_das@redwood.example
Cc: Anika Patel <anika.patel@medtechlabs.io>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 14:03:00 +0000
Subject: Follow-up + data handling constraints for private pilot

Thanks again for the call today — good overview. A few items we need clarified for our security and procurement teams before we can sign off on a private (VPC/on-prem) pilot: 

- PII classification: We will ingest patient contact info and limited PHI metadata. Can Redwood support configuration to drop or tokenise specific fields before they touch the inference runtime?
- Retention windows: Our legal team requires that any logs or request artifacts containing identifiers be retained no longer than 30 days for the pilot, and optionally zero retention for production. Can that be enforced per-project?
- Audit/logging: We need an auditable trail of model version, request timestamp, and who triggered the inference. What granularity do your audit logs provide, and can logs be exported to our Splunk instance (SPLK ingest)?
- Air-gapped/on-prem installer: We need an installer that does not require outbound internet during runtime. Is the private deployment fully airgap-capable, and what console/instrumentation options remain available to us?
- Network egress: If we do limited egress (only to our internal S3 and monitoring endpoints), what are the supported egress control primitives and IP whitelisting approaches?

Next steps: can we get a short written response addressing the five bullets above and a draft scope for a 4-week pilot? Procurement is targeting a decision by 2027-05-03.

Thanks,
Evan Brooks
Director of Cloud Ops
MedTech Labs

Hi Evan — thanks, great list. Summarizing answers below at a high level; Prio (SE) and Marcus (Infra) have added notes and a diagram. We'll follow with a short 30–45m technical deep-dive this week to lock the pilot scope.

1) PII handling: Yes — private deployments can be configured with preprocessing hooks to redact or tokenise fields before they reach the model. We support JSON-path rules and a simple config map for field-level redaction. If you need deterministic tokenisation, we can surface an HMAC-based tokeniser that keeps the original unrecoverable.

2) Retention windows: Per-project retention policies are supported. For private deployments you can set request artifacts (inputs, model outputs, KV caches) to 0/7/30/90 days. We also support a "zero retention" mode where logs with content are never persisted; only minimal audit metadata is written.

3) Audit/logging: Audit logs include request id, model version, route, timestamps, and actor metadata (API key or user). We can stream logs to Splunk over HTTPS via a forwarder or push to your S3, with optional KMS-wrapped encryption.

4) Air-gap & installer: We offer an on-prem installer (OCI images + orchestration manifests) that supports air-gapped runtime: the control plane can be run in your VPC, and runtime nodes do not require outbound internet for inference. Admin tooling (console) needs a control plane endpoint; you can host that in your management VPC.

5) Network egress: Egress is configurable per-route. Supported controls include CNI network policies (k8s), outbound IP whitelisting, and an egress gateway in the deployment to restrict external destinations. For truly zero egress we can disable external calls and only allow your S3/monitoring endpoints.

Attachments: redwood-private-deployment-security.pdf (security brief) — Marcus attached a network sketch in his reply.

Proposed next steps:
- Technical deep-dive (30–45m) with your security + infra + dev leads — suggested times: Tue/Wed 16:00–18:00 CEST.
- Draft pilot scope (4 weeks) and statement of work — I'll share a starter doc for comments.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Follow-up + data handling constraints for private pilot

Hi Evan — adding a few technical specifics below to Kim's summary and attaching the network sketch.

- Field-level redaction/tokenisation: we support an inline preprocessor (Lua-like) that runs before serialization to the model. It can drop fields or replace values with stable tokens. Configuration is stored in the control plane and can be versioned per-pipeline.

- KV cache & model artifacts: KV caches are ephemeral by default; for pilot we recommend setting cache TTL to 0 if you want no persistent cached context. Model artifacts are stored locally on node disks and can be mounted on encrypted volumes.

- Splunk export: we can forward compressed log batches via HTTPS with HEC token. If you prefer push-to-S3, we can sign objects with customer KMS.

- Airgap process notes: install is done via our packaged tarball + local registry import. Telemetry (optional) can be configured to write to your internal metrics stack (Prometheus + Grafana). The only external reach required is the initial license validation (we can provide an offline license file for the pilot).

- Egress gateway: sample options are to run our egress gateway in your DMZ and lock outbound to only your internal endpoints; we can provide iptables/Cilium examples.

See attached: network-diagram-v1.png (sketch of recommended VPC boundaries and egress gateway), pilot-action-items.xlsx (starter checklist). Happy to walk through this during the call.

—Prio

Thanks Kim and Prio — that covers most of our questions. Two follow-ups from security/procurement:

1) Metadata-only logs: for the pilot we'd prefer inputs/outputs to not be stored; only the minimal metadata (request id, model version, timestamp) should be kept. Can you confirm the "zero retention" mode will still provide sufficient diagnostic telemetry so we can troubleshoot failures without payloads?

2) Legal & procurement: do you have a short one-page summary we can share with our procurement counsel describing data flows (who has access to PII in the deployment, where artifacts are stored, retention controls)? If possible we'd like that by 2027-04-26.

Also — procurement asked whether Redwood is willing to sign a minimal data processing addendum (DPA) for the pilot period. Procurement email is procurement@medtechlabs.io — happy to loop them in.

Best,
Evan
